headline: High risk of shared-filesystem prompt injection and write conflicts; default pairwise use can also cascade unverified edits.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Mentat reads and writes filesystem content and shares state with other instances via filesystem; Plandex also reads/writes a project directory and plan-local sandbox. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if one agent consumes the other's files. No clipboard/MCP bridge is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF Mentat reads files that Plandex wrote into the shared project directory
IF Plandex ingests Mentat-generated diffs or notes as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Require manual review of any file produced by the other agent
Use read-only mounts for one agent during the other's run
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and both have broad network egress plus model-provider API calls, so shared workspace content can flow into remote inference backends. Mentat explicitly handles model provider API keys, and Plandex uses a cloud or self-hosted server; the pair can therefore expose code and secrets if run on the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same repository containing secrets
IF either agent uploads file contents from the shared workspace to its backend
mitigations: Remove secrets from the workspace before running
Use separate repositories or clones
Restrict network egress during one agent's run
Rotate any exposed API keys after use
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret redaction

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can write the filesystem and modify git state, and Mentat shares state via filesystem while Plandex shares state via a backend. In a shared repo, concurrent edits and git mutations can race or overwrite each other without locking, matching the high-risk overlap indicator.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git checkout
IF either agent auto-applies changes while the other is still planning or editing
mitigations: Run only one agent per checkout
Serialize git writes with a manual lock
Keep Plandex in review-only mode
Export patches instead of direct commits
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Mentat produces diff-based edit proposals, and Plandex uses review-then-apply with optional auto-apply mode. If Plandex treats Mentat's output as authoritative, unverified edits can cascade into applied changes, especially when both agents are allowed to modify the same files.
conditions: IF Plandex auto-applies or applies with minimal review
IF Mentat's proposed diffs are fed directly into Plandex as trusted input
mitigations: Require human approval before apply
Disable auto-apply mode
Have Plandex re-derive changes from source files
Compare proposed diffs against a second review pass
requires-engineering: add validation of upstream agent outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding tools with source-code data classes and no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. The only concrete compliance concern is that both handle model-provider API keys and may send code to external services, but the pairwise compliance gap is not specified enough to justify more than low.
conditions: IF the workspace contains regulated data such as PHI or EU PII
IF either configured backend retains prompts or code beyond the operator's policy
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the shared workspace
Review provider retention settings
Use self-hosted backends where available
Rotate API keys after the session
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
